name: Temporal brow lift

lead: A temporal brow lift raises the outer part of the eyebrow through incisions hidden in the hair-bearing temple area. Patients seek it to lift a drooping brow tail and open the eye area, and looksmaxxing communities group it with eye-area surgery.

Tissue at the brow tail is released and re-fixed higher at the temple, by subcutaneous, endoscopic or combined methods. The lift is visible after surgery and is documented in surgical case series and technique comparisons; surgeons disagree about the best approach.

paras: It is done by a plastic or facial surgeon, usually under anaesthesia, sometimes combined with eyelid surgery. Swelling and bruising settle over a couple of weeks, and the brow position is judged once healing is done.
Reported risks include injury to the frontal branch of the facial nerve, numbness, hair loss at the incisions, infection, bleeding and recurrence of brow drop with some methods.

angle.text: People want a lifted outer brow and a more open eye area. Surgeons release tissue at the brow tail and fix it higher at the temple through hidden incisions. The lift is visible after healing and is documented in surgical series.

lead: A temporal (lateral) brow lift is a surgical procedure that raises the outer part of the eyebrow using incisions placed in the hair-bearing temple area. It is one of several brow-lifting approaches that also include coronal, endoscopic, direct and internal (transblepharoplasty) lifts.[1] Patients seek it to lift a drooping brow tail and open the eye area; looksmaxxing communities group it with eye-area surgery.

Studies describe subcutaneous and endoscopic temporal variants, various fixation techniques and results in case series.[2][3][4] Evidence is mainly surgical case series and comparative studies, and surgeons disagree about the best approach.[5]

paras: Wikipedia lists temporal lifts among the brow lift types, with endoscopic methods using small incisions and a camera, and coronal lifts having fallen out of favour.[1] Variants include a subcutaneous temporal lift under local anaesthesia and a combined endoscopic and temporal approach.[3][6] Different fixation techniques have been compared.[7]

A 2019 report of ten-year outcomes of endoscopic temporal brow lift described the indications and technique; a combined endoscopic and temporal approach was presented as a way to reduce the high recurrence rate of endoscopic lifts.[3] A 2010 report described a subcutaneous temporal lift under local anaesthesia for periorbital rejuvenation.[6] A 2018 study compared temporal brow lift with internal browpexy in women undergoing upper blepharoplasty for lateral brow lifting.[8] A 2015 study compared three fixation techniques.[7] A cadaver study found the frontal branch of the facial nerve runs in a plane at risk in the superolateral brow area.[4]

Botulinum toxin A injections directed at brow depressors have been reported to raise the lateral brow in a 22-patient case series, described as a temporal brow lift.[2] A 2026 article argues against the subcutaneous approach, illustrating surgeon disagreement.[5]

Wikipedia states complications of brow lifts are generally rare and minor in trained hands; hair loss is most common after endoscopic lifts, and numbness after direct lifts. Infection and bleeding are possible with any surgery.[1] The frontal branch of the facial nerve is the structure of concern in temporal dissection.[4]

timeline.event: First documented medical discussion of forehead lifting by Erich Lexer (per Wikipedia).[1]
Cadaver study of the frontalis nerve in temporal brow lift.[4]
